concepts.definition: F11 is the source's foundation-to-law family for change entry, classification and reuse, ambiguity governance and shared-interface migration. Its additional instance premises are changing specifications during work, reports of every kind arriving at one product, shared interfaces with several producers and consumers, and decisions either permitted under policy or reserved to human authority. The cited standing is P0 recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 independent; P4b derived from P0 and P2 with non-reacquirable step-produced facts; P5 derived from P0 and P6 with the open-world premise.

grounding.quote:
Standing of
 the commitments cited

concepts.label: Change management and ambiguity foundation family

conditions: A report may represent substantive change.
concepts.definition: Universal intake triage is the common entry for bugs, feature requests, issues, regressions, operator findings, release blockers and scenario failures. It determines substantive-change status, affected product and scope, lawful change class, lawful constitutional re-entry, affected downstream surfaces and evidence, and release-scope fit or repricing.

grounding.quote:
There is one front door for substantive change. The intake label does not
 determine the process class:

concepts.label: Universal intake triage

concepts.definition: The minimum declared change states are: goal_reprice, changing bounded work-wave focus, re-entering Goals and flowing through Intent, Product, Requirements, Design, Code and Evidence where that focus changes deeper truth; intent_reprice, directional or scope change, re-entering Intent and flowing through Product, Requirements, Design, Code and Evidence; product_reprice, changed current product realisation with stable directional intent, re-entering Product and flowing through Requirements, Design, Code and Evidence; requirement_reprice, changed constitutional truth with stable project direction, re-entering Requirements and flowing through Design, Code and Evidence; design_reframe, changed realisation structure with stable active intent and requirement truth, re-entering Design and flowing through Code and Evidence; realization_refactor, local code, configuration or attribute change without intended constitutional or structural change, re-entering only the realised surface with no upstream flow and requiring proof of no upstream drift.

grounding.quote: | `realization_refactor` | local code, configuration or attribute change with no intended constitutional or structural change | the realised surface only | nothing upstream; it must prove no upstream drift |

concepts.label: Declared change classes and flows

concepts.definition: C denotes reproducible facts and declared-rule application in one reusable intake classification. Relation states changed, unchanged and unknown; identity changes added, removed or retained with changed value; and evidence states covered, missing, stale, ambiguous and outside scope are classification facts, not evaluation results or core values.

grounding.quote:
C denotes reproducible facts and declared rule
application; J denotes residual semantic or materiality judgment; O denotes
a ruling reserved to its actual owner.

concepts.label: Computed classification C

conditions: Semantic sufficiency, materiality, intended meaning or necessity remains unresolved by sufficient declared premises.
concepts.definition: J is residual semantic or materiality judgment, kept distinct from reproducible classification facts and owner-reserved rulings. No residual judgment is invented when declared rules settle the question.

grounding.quote: J denotes residual semantic or materiality judgment;

concepts.label: Residual judgment J

conditions: A decision is reserved to its actual owner.
concepts.definition: O denotes an owner-reserved ruling. C, J and O annotations grant no authority and introduce no calculus kind, runtime, classifier interface or mandatory document.

grounding.quote: The annotations grant no authority,

concepts.label: Owner ruling O

conditions: A declared change span is under assessment.
concepts.definition: The consistency gate applies the TICKETS-owned condition-based closure rule to obligations declared for the change span, requiring upstream sufficiency, downstream consistency with active truth, and proof of active intended behaviour.

grounding.quote: its required coverage.

concepts.label: Consistency gate

concepts.definition: A sprint is a bounded execution-control surface under existing goals, intent, product, requirement and design authority. It batches and coordinates work, prices proof cost and forces close review without adding a constitutional layer.

grounding.quote:
A sprint is a bounded execution-control surface, not a new layer in the
constitutional chain

concepts.label: Method sprint boundary

concepts.definition: Work-carrier selection follows required lifetime: a durable ticket for identity across sessions, a sprint-local entry for traceability whose only value is inside the batch, or a run/return record for work confined to one activation. TICKETS owns the carrier model and smallest-lawful-carrier selection.

grounding.quote: The carrier of a work item is selected for its required lifetime:

concepts.label: Lifetime-based carrier selection

concepts.definition: Four source-defined procedures cover substantive intake, feature introduction/change, project bootstrap or requirement-surface repricing, and gaps revealed by real use cases. Their ordering, conditional updates and design acceptance boundaries are represented as requirements rather than executed procedures.

grounding.quote:
only then treat the work as implementation, repricing or
release-bound change.

concepts.label: Change-management procedures

conditions: Under the selected complete basis.
concepts.definition: The substrate-neutral context urn:stdo:bounded-context:ambiguity-governance governs progressive disambiguation. Goals narrow priority and work-wave focus; intent direction and scope; product realisation shape and terms; requirements constitutional obligation; tenant/stack choice executable realisation class; design structural interpretation; implementation local detail. Major ambiguity materially affects architecture, stack, product boundary, execution/deployment admissibility, public contract or downstream law; micro ambiguity is a local choice within an already-governed design boundary.

grounding.quote: `urn:stdo:bounded-context:ambiguity-governance`

concepts.label: Ambiguity governance

conditions: Declared policy permits bounded processing to carry or resolve declared ambiguity.
concepts.definition: urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:lawful-probabilistic-processing names bounded non-human processing permitted by policy. A person carrying or deciding ambiguity under policy without human-adjudication admission is governed by this processing's policy and recording requirements; performer identity does not determine operation kind.

grounding.quote:
is bounded non-human processing permitted by declared policy to carry or
resolve declared ambiguity.

concepts.label: Lawful probabilistic processing

conditions: Authority admits explicit human judgment to resolve declared ambiguity where policy or risk appetite requires it.
concepts.definition: urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:human-adjudication names explicitly admitted human judgment. Admission makes the operation adjudication; merely relaying, recording or performing a step does not.

grounding.quote:
That admission makes an operation
human adjudication.

concepts.label: Human adjudication

concepts.definition: Recursive product lineage distinguishes substrate, development product, source project, release cut, product, install, artifact and product definition. The product definition is the source project's present-tense surface, distinct from the released artifact and active builder. Immutable v<version>-rc.<n> identifies an exact release cut; mutable v<version> discovers the highest-ordinal published cut. Calculus, subject interpretation and carrier encoding maintain independent content identities, judgments, supersession and proof obligations.

grounding.quote:
The only exact operative release identifier is the immutable release-cut
tag `v<version>-rc.<n>`

concepts.label: Product lineage and release identities

conditions: A reusable method change is proposed.
concepts.definition: Shared-method adoption expresses authority causality in this order: incident/review evidence, shared-method intake, one owning standard, consistency and independent review, human-authority acceptance, one complete released STDO version, explicit consumer selection, and consumer-owned realisation/evidence. It prescribes neither an intake workflow nor an artifact set.

grounding.quote:
The chain states authority causality. It prescribes no intake workflow and
no artifact set

concepts.label: Shared method adoption and propagation

conditions: A shared contract or carrier materially governs one or more listed truth-bearing functions.
concepts.definition: A core interface materially governs runtime closure, reporting/status truth, topology/frame progression, proof/qualification outcomes, event/projection semantics, identity/binding resolution, or provider/resolver behaviour. A change capable of altering how multiple surfaces determine present truth is a core-interface change.

grounding.quote:
If changing the
interface can alter how multiple surfaces decide what is true now, it is a
core interface change

concepts.label: Core interface

conditions: A change alters a load-bearing contract, carrier, resolver, provider, projection law, closure law or other interface shared by multiple surfaces.
concepts.definition: Core-interface migration is constitutional migration rather than an ordinary local patch. It replaces authoritative contract truth, migrates every impacted producer and consumer, and follows downstream effects until superseded closure law is gone.

grounding.quote:
the work is handled as a constitutional migration, not as incremental
patching

concepts.label: Constitutional core-interface migration

conditions: The project stays on the same implementation line and replaces authoritative source truth in place.
concepts.definition: Inside-out hard-break migration is one of two lawful constitutional strategies. It proceeds from the source carrier outward through deliberate breaks and repairs; bounded evolution is a rebuttable strategy-selection presumption, not a third strategy.
concepts.label: Inside-out hard-break strategy

conditions: A project intentionally abandons prior constitutional shape and re-derives on a new branch, version line or methodology basis.
concepts.definition: Fundamental migration is a constitutional reset. Fundamental re-adoption applies to a major rewrite on a materially different implementation basis, such as runtime, carrier, type system, substrate or realisation tree; prior implementation becomes reference material. Inherited constitutional material has adoption states adopted, superseded, deferred or orphaned. Inherited implementation is carry_across, materially unchanged and explicitly re-adopted; redundant, no longer needed; or rewrite, still needed but rebuilt under new requirements and design.

grounding.quote:
A fundamental migration is a constitutional reset, not an in-place
refactor.

the prior implementation is moved sideways
and treated as reference material, not live authority.

concepts.label: Fundamental migration and re-adoption

conditions: An affected product outcome is considered for promotion.
concepts.definition: The acceptance path is the outcome's full causal closure: every admitted entrypoint, producer, consumer, resolver, fallback, shared state surface, event, projection and proof surface capable of changing, interpreting or closing it. Singular authority concerns this entire closure, not one successful trace.

grounding.quote:
Singular authority means
one governing authority across that closure, not one selected successful
trace.

concepts.label: Outcome acceptance path

conditions: An intermediate product outcome is considered within an open migration.
concepts.definition: A product slice has identity and acceptance criteria derived from the product, every causally applicable live requirement, accepted design relation and retained predecessor claim. Slice promotion is distinct from migration, qualification or release closure.
concepts.label: Intermediate product slice

concepts.definition: Projections, reports, status views and topology views reflect an authoritative carrier while remaining downstream of its truth and closure law.

grounding.quote:
Projections, reports, status views and topology views may reflect the
authoritative carrier; they do not become a second closure surface

concepts.label: Downstream projection

conditions: Refactor or migration affects mutable implementation surfaces.
concepts.definition: A transformation wave is the changing implementation across its declared affected scope. An inside-out migration wave is an ordered set of hard breaks over one interface family, not a mode permitting competing authority.

grounding.quote:
Refactor and migration should be understood as a transformation wave over
mutable
implementation surfaces
The migration wave is the ordered set of those breaks;

concepts.label: Transformation and migration wave

conditions: Construction is delegated to a probabilistic or agentic worker.
concepts.definition: Bounded execution applies ACTIVATION's step: accepted governing basis, bounded affected relations, selected computational relations, delegated execution and decision grants, construction/self-review, required independent live-surface assessment, owner disposition accept/local_repair/re_enter/reject, exact accepted checkpoint, and next already-authorised bounded action. Candidate availability, assessment results and owner disposition are separate results; preservation, progress and completion are distinct construction claims.

grounding.quote:
a candidate that is available or
assessed is not thereby accepted

concepts.label: Bounded construction step

conditions: A realisation claim requires closure evidence.
concepts.definition: Realisation evidence includes an authority trace, realisation proof, negative proof where drift is plausible, and a present-tense statement of residual open pressure. This is an application of the TICKETS closure condition, not an additional closure condition.
concepts.label: Evidence for a realisation claim

concepts.definition: An ADR records a design decision boundary answering what design choice makes the acceptance criteria true. Each ADR file remains constitutional source; an optional registry is a read model. ADR history is append-only subject to explicit retirement.

grounding.quote: ADRs are written per decision boundary, not per requirement file;

concepts.label: Architecture decision record

conditions: Every product built with the described method.
concepts.definition: A build tenant is an independent project-owned HOW realisation of a product's WHAT. One WHAT has one or more independent tenants regardless of physical layout. A registry entry locates the tenant and is not its binding; tenant-local realisation remains derivative until governing truth is ratified in specification.

grounding.quote:
A build tenant is one independent, project-owned HOW realisation of a
  product's WHAT.

concepts.label: Build tenant

concepts.definition: A product's requirements calculus comprises its WHAT obligations, permitted outcomes, and rules for refining and composing the work that realises it.

grounding.quote:
The requirements calculus of a product is the set of obligations its
  WHAT states, the outcomes it permits, and its rules for refining and
  composing the work that realises it.

concepts.label: Requirements calculus

conditions: Operations, effects and resources are described insofar as material to obligations.
concepts.definition: A computational calculus declares executable operations, composition laws, permitted transformations, effects and resource behaviour.

grounding.quote: A computational calculus is a declared set of executable operations,

concepts.label: Computational calculus

concepts.definition: An execution environment concretely performs operations through a technology stack, a human process of people, roles, documents, communication channels and decision procedures, or both. Operation kind is what an operation does, such as construct, assess, relay, record, measure or decide, together with the authority it requires.

grounding.quote:
An execution environment is the concrete means that performs those
  operations:

concepts.label: Execution environment and operation kinds

concepts.definition: A tenant binding consists of a calculus binding from requirements calculus to computational calculus and an execution binding from computational calculus to execution environment. Both are tenant-owned design and realisation, declared in existing design/realisation surfaces and recorded as design decisions without a further mandatory carrier. Algorithmic, informational and computational accounts remain distinct across the binding.

grounding.quote: A tenant's build-tenant binding has two parts:

concepts.label: Build-tenant binding

concepts.definition: The source-disposition register records claimed conservation, generalisation, relocation, new law and proposed supersession of predecessor rows. Anchors point to predecessor material and loci to receiving sections; routes are provenance, not imported authority. Conserved rows are stated to be restated by their receiving members.

grounding.quote:
Every conserved row is
restated in the receiving member's own text; a route is provenance only.

concepts.label: Predecessor source-disposition register

concepts.definition: TICKETS is a tier-2 member owning goals, tickets, sprints, comments and execution contracts as one carrier model; layout/bindings; sprint and ticket mechanics; triage/class recording/upward propagation; carrier selection and carrier-side contract admission; execution/verification separation; J/O continuity; closure/reuse; test-case authority; migration ticket declaration/checklist/review; one-truth projections; recommended shapes and operating mode. It is the T area and realises FOUNDATIONS, ACTIVATION and EVALUATION, without redefining their law.

grounding.quote:
Tier 2. Owns the work carriers of the method: goals, tickets, sprints,
comments and execution contracts as one model;

concepts.label: TICKETS member

concepts.definition: The goals carrier is the current epic layer located by ticketing.goals, default GOALS.md. It states the active work wave and present priorities, broader than a ticket and narrower and more current than intent; it is not durable execution tracking.

grounding.quote:
Goals are
not the durable unit of execution tracking

concepts.label: Goals carrier

conditions: Work needs independent durable identity, including features, bugs, spikes and chores.
concepts.definition: A ticket is one enduring, typed work record and the source of truth for its work unit, durable across sessions. One Markdown file is the default carrier; bugs and features share this system.

grounding.quote: Tickets are the enduring work records. Each ticket is one durable record,

concepts.label: Durable ticket

concepts.definition: A TICKETS sprint is one manifest for a bounded execution batch and its explicit close review, located by optional ticketing.sprints.root, default .ai-workspace/sprints/. It batches authority references, closure law, evidence expectations and local compliance debt. It can contain durable tickets, manifest-local iterations, or both; its batch authority is not constitutional authority.

grounding.quote: Sprints are not constitutional authority:

concepts.label: Sprint work carrier

concepts.definition: Comments are POSTING_GUIDE posts for ideas, strategy, reviews, handoffs, closure summaries and reasoned decisions. ticketing.comments.root locates the message board, default .ai-workspace/comments/. Comments have no task-status authority or decision authority of their own.

grounding.quote:
A decision recorded in a
comment takes its authority from the surface that owns the decision, once
it is adopted there

concepts.label: Comment carrier

concepts.definition: An execution contract is the admitted run-scoped execution function derived from a ticket, a sprint manifest plus included ticket/iteration, or intake when no durable or sprint-local identity is needed. It lives for one run, unlike a ticket across sessions/work waves or a sprint through its batch and close review; it is neither a rival backlog nor a second planning surface.

grounding.quote:
Execution contracts are not a
rival backlog or a second planning surface

concepts.label: Run-scoped execution contract

conditions: A ticket uses closure-bearing milestones.
concepts.definition: A milestone is a bounded work claim with stable identity, dependencies, current state, required evidence and explicit relation to ticket closure. Several milestones may belong to one ticket without creating several tickets.

grounding.quote:
Each milestone has stable identity, a bounded claim,
relevant dependencies, current state, required evidence, and an explicit
relation to ticket closure

concepts.label: Closure-bearing milestone

concepts.definition: Product-definition bindings locate carrier authority: ticketing.goals for epics; optional ticketing.sprints.root for batches/close review; ticketing.tickets.lanes.backlog, .active and .completed for ticket authority; ticketing.comments.root for publication/discussion. stdo_default.json supplies the starter layout with specification/GOALS.md and .ai-workspace/{sprints,tickets/{backlog,active,completed},comments/<agent-id>}. The definition locates carriers without owning their ticket/comment content.

grounding.quote:
The definition locates these carriers and
does not own their ticket or comment content.
The starter file layout (P2, P3; rc.2 #default-layout):

concepts.label: Carrier bindings and default layout

concepts.definition: Each sprint has one durable manifest record. A Markdown file is default; other bound carriers preserve identity, required fields, history, closure law and one-truth relation. A local filename should have a stable ID and short slug; the dated SPRINT examples are recommendations.

grounding.quote: Each sprint has one durable manifest record;

concepts.label: Durable sprint manifest

concepts.definition: Minimum sprint statuses are active, admitting iteration within the boundary; closing, freezing new iteration while close review/paydown classification run; closed, review finished and remaining debt accepted, ticketed, repriced or removed; and superseded, an incorrect boundary replaced by a new authority surface, sprint or ticket set. Optional planned/cancelled states do not replace close review.

grounding.quote:
A project may add `planned` or
`cancelled`; those states do not replace close review.

concepts.label: Sprint status domain

conditions: The governing method allows local proof deferral and all escrow conditions hold.
concepts.definition: Compliance escrow is visible local compliance debt held by a sprint rather than acceptance. It does not satisfy method, release or product closure until paid down, accepted under governing method, or repriced.

grounding.quote:
Deferred compliance is not
silent debt: it is escrow held by the sprint,

concepts.label: Sprint compliance escrow

conditions: A family-table consumer applies a cited rule.

grounding.quote:
Each consumer applies the rule and decides nothing the owning section does
not (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: The ten foundation rows account for §§4, 5 and 7 and do not let consumers decide beyond their owning rules. Named policy/domain choices remain distinguished from claimed consequences: six classes and four procedures; case-specific smallest frame configuration under REFERENCE_FRAME; C/J/O annotations, step order and C inputs; sprint requirements and close triggers with profile-specific escrow suitability; project risk appetite and member-owned ambiguity distinctions; migration strategies, evolution presumption and old-path classes; inside-out order; inherited-implementation classes. Fundamental re-adoption selection belongs to the human owner of the product boundary.
constraints.uncertainty: Referenced foundation derivations, consumer bodies and some domain definitions are not supplied.

conditions: Any substantive intake arrives.

grounding.quote:
No bug, feature, issue or other intake bypasses this triage by going
straight to code, tests or release handling.

constraints.statement: Perform all six determinations before code, tests or release handling; the evidence-impact component is S_Δ over I(Δ). Diagnose among defective realisation, inadequate governing requirement/design, inaccurate predictive model and insufficient observation. Route each supported repair to the cause's owner, never infer the route from its intake label. Severity and priority follow TICKETS-owned policies; a bug list projects existing work state. This applies ACTIVATION's diagnosis relation rather than creating another.
constraints.uncertainty: The impact-cover formalism and TICKETS severity/priority policies are referenced but not defined in the supplied source.

conditions: Triage triangulates a failure.

grounding.quote:
a counterexample that
one frame finds survives the join, and a frame planned and not applied
leaves its diagnosis open, never ruled out.

constraints.statement: Use the smallest sufficient applicable reference-frame configuration on the same subject and basis. Each frame tests candidate diagnoses against its own material workspace variables, governing relations and evidence; combine results with each diagnosis retained as predicate, preserving counterexamples, uncertainty and unresolved alternatives. The exposing frame need not contain the cause; relabelled duplicate analysis adds no causal evidence. Identify the smallest sufficient lawful repair scope and apply counterexample localisation where required. Prescribe neither reviewer count nor a new review round, while preserving required independence. Diagnosis grants no repair effects and does not prove governing meaning must change; existing sufficient law may instead require candidate correction.
constraints.uncertainty: Frame applicability, conjunction and required localisation depend on referenced owners.

conditions: Substantive work begins.

grounding.quote:
Triage records the change intent, the class, the re-entry point and when
triage occurred, wherever substantive work begins.

constraints.statement: A smaller change may re-enter below Goals only with an explicit assertion that no upstream constitutional surface changes. An absent declared class is process drift. Only the owner accepts a changed governing relation; acceptance within the acting frame violates the rule regardless of delta size. Record change intent, class, re-entry and triage time; TICKETS records the class on the carrier.

conditions: A declared class or classification fact is consumed by evaluation.

grounding.quote:
a declared class is never combined as an
evaluation result
classification fact is never combined as an evaluation result

constraints.statement: Declared classes and computed facts map to no core value and never substitute for evaluation results. A consuming evaluation returns its own core value for its predicate, keeping consumed unknowns unknown. realization_refactor does not prove no upstream drift; covered evidence or an unchanged relation does not prove satisfied. A TICKETS close classification naming a layer is an evaluation result for its own predicate and carries the re-entry class only as its domain outcome.
constraints.uncertainty: The complete core-value mapping and close-classification mapping are external references.

conditions: An explicitly selected source, worksite or qualification capability produces C.

grounding.quote:
A missing
candidate or missing evidence is an input state, not a claim that nothing
changed.

constraints.statement: C covers the exact request and desired outcome; known targets/effects; operation grant/work lifetime; product definition/governing basis; baseline/available candidate; declared relations; accepted design/trace bindings; evidence; and applicable rules. Its output identifies producer and procedure revision, inputs, result, scope, source routes, reproduction relation, unknowns and invalidators. Missing candidate or evidence remains an input state rather than evidence of no change.

conditions: The computed classification exposes its analysis.
exceptions: A rename is not removal plus addition when the owner supplies an identity-preserving relation.

grounding.quote: The computed result exposes four things, in this order:

constraints.statement: Expose, in order: (1) authority traversal following explicit source, ownership, dependency, composition and projection declarations from affected targets/effects; record every reached layer/owner, exact basis, changed/unchanged/unknown relation, traversed edges and unresolved frontier, including root/authority/grant changes despite equal public bytes; absent edges prove no irrelevance and uncertain materiality remains J. (2) Public delta over the complete relevant serialised member universe under owning declaration/projection, including helper/generated dependencies; enumerate added/removed identities and every retained member with changed typed value or bytes and exact before/after values; missing candidate, incomplete enumeration, ambiguous identity or unavailable projection makes the affected delta unknown, and membership equality proves no value equality. (3) Accepted-design coverage joining changed bytes/relations to explicit accepted scope, traces and acceptance evidence; distinguish covered/missing/stale/ambiguous/outside-scope evidence; filename, artifact listing or digest alone proves no coverage; trace coverage is C while semantic sufficiency remains J. (4) Rule-determined treatment using only declared rules with sufficient facts, recording owners, matched predicates and consequences; expose smallest lawful re-entry, next action, evidence/assessment, reserved ruling and carrier lifetime while preserving conflicts/missing premises. Labels and filenames cannot select routes; settled rules require no invented J.

conditions: A public delta or other nonconformance is found.

grounding.quote:
Candidate
behaviour cannot author its own target law

constraints.statement: Nonconformance alone does not require contract change. If governing law remains sufficient for the authorised outcome, reject the candidate or repair it locally within grant. Re-enter the actual governing owner when the explicitly selected desired outcome needs changed meaning or an applicable assessment establishes governing insufficiency. C determines this only from sufficient declared premises; unresolved intended meaning/necessity remains J and reserved decisions remain O.

conditions: Treatment is unknown, evidence changes, a route is mistaken, or effects have uncertain completion.

grounding.quote:
is reconciled as ACTIVATION §5 states before any retry
or dependent action

constraints.statement: Unknown treatment withholds dependent reliance/promotion, not unrelated authorised work. An existing bounded construction/evidence grant may permit the cheapest useful discriminator, including a first candidate, without claiming conformance; that grant retains its own exact subject, territory, operations and stop conditions. Update affected C before dependent effects or promotion rely on new evidence. Correct a mistaken route at its smallest affected owner, preserving original cause, attempted subject, observed effect state and valid progress. Retry needs applicable outcome, authority and safe-recovery conditions. completion_unknown, and not_effected whose end is unestablished, cannot silently mean no effect and must be reconciled before retry or dependent action.
constraints.uncertainty: The detailed reconciliation and safe-recovery rules belong to unsupplied ACTIVATION sections.

conditions: A role, conversation or resumption reuses C, or its basis changes.

grounding.quote:
the wider frontier is recomputed where
independence is unproved

constraints.statement: Reuse valid C only after exact-applicability checking. Before reliance, invalidate affected claims when request, candidate, owner/root relation, projection, design trace/acceptance, applied rule, configuration or material evidence changes; a changed basis or declared revising observation also invalidates. Preserve predecessor/successor identities, changed inputs, surviving facts and affected J dependencies, recomputing the wider frontier where independence is unproved. ACTIVATION owns reuse/invalidation; TICKETS owns carriers and recorded J/O continuity.
constraints.uncertainty: External owners' detailed continuity rules are not supplied.

conditions: Closure is considered for a declared change span.

grounding.quote:
If that proof is
missing the change remains open even if one local artifact already looks
correct.

constraints.statement: No gate closes while affected active surfaces are internally inconsistent. Prove upstream sufficiency, downstream non-contradiction and active intended behaviour rather than stale precedent. Material counterexamples to mandatory constraints, required judgments/rulings without closed results, and obligations with no evidence each block closure and remain recorded by kind. Review events, passing aggregates, completed artifacts and status changes cannot substitute for the obligation/evidence conjunction. Reuse follows ACTIVATION and carrier state follows TICKETS. In ticketed code/test mismatches, implementation is evidence, not authority; reconcile through admitted ticket, intake, lawful re-entry and governing requirement, design, module, carrier or closure surface, under TICKETS/ASSURANCE test authority.
constraints.uncertainty: Full closure, reuse and test-authority laws are referenced rather than supplied.

conditions: A sprint is used.

grounding.quote: A lawful sprint states at least:

constraints.statement: State at least served goal/work wave, upstream authority surfaces, admitted scope, excluded product/requirement/design/runtime/data-contract/governance boundaries, expected classes, any deferrable local proof/compliance debt, closure trigger/law and debt paydown/repricing path. The sprint cannot create, supersede, weaken or override existing authority. Proof-cost deferral is lawful only while local, visible, bounded and repayable; escrow is not acceptance and closes no method/release/product obligation until paid down, explicitly accepted under governing method, or repriced upstream.

conditions: Sprint closure is recommended or performed, or product-truth change is discovered.

grounding.quote: the sprint manifest does not authorise landing it;

constraints.statement: Close may be recommended on timebox expiry, reached scope, changed-surface cost making review cheaper than iteration, review uncertainty making continuation unsafe, or gaps suggesting the wrong container. Close is forensic reconciliation, not automatic approval: compare accumulated work/evidence with authority, classify each gap, accept compliant work, open local-debt paydown and escalate authority drift through lawful classes. Discovered goal, intent, product, requirement, design, runtime, data-contract, governance or other product-truth change must be split, escalated, repriced or carried as explicit paydown. TICKETS owns mechanics; profiles may define domain-appropriate escrow optimisation.

conditions: Substantive work begins, regardless of its carrier.

grounding.quote:
The triage fields are required wherever substantive work begins; a ticket
per change is not

constraints.statement: Require triage fields wherever substantive work starts; do not impose one ticket per change. Select the carrier by lifetime under the TICKETS-owned smallest-lawful-carrier rule.

conditions: Any substantive intake, or feature introduction/change.

grounding.quote:
reconcile
design, implementation and tests before promotion or closure;

constraints.statement: First triage/classify, determine lawful re-entry and affected downstream consistency span; only then treat work as implementation, repricing or release-bound. For features: update Goals if work wave/overriding concerns change, Intent if purpose/scope changes, Product if realisation/terms/boundaries/end-state shape changes; make invariant requirements explicit as product decomposition, including lifecycle obligations or named gaps, and categorise each new/changed requirement. Design owns structural HOW. Under the design profile, apply decision-completeness: co-evolve design/code/tests only under its predicate; otherwise accept the smallest causally closed affected design set before retained implementation establishes unresolved, contradictory or materially non-equivalent relations. Outside that profile, co-evolution is permitted only without unresolved material design decisions; otherwise accept affected design before retained implementation establishes them, ADRs being valid design. Write scenarios for capability claims needing operational proof and other appropriate evidence for non-capability requirements. Prefer declarative problem/acceptance expression before imperative mechanism. Check sufficiency across Goals→Intent→Product→Requirements→Design→Implementation; record/govern major ambiguity by declared risk; develop under selected design; reconcile design/code/tests before promotion/closure and use events, projection and delta to verify requirement satisfaction.
constraints.uncertainty: The design-profile co-evolution predicate and category taxonomy are not supplied.

conditions: Project bootstrap, requirement-surface repricing, or a gap revealed by a real use case.

grounding.quote:
only after that surface
exists should downstream design and implementation be treated as
constitutionally grounded.

writing new
goals or intent only where the work wave, direction or scope changes.

constraints.statement: For bootstrap/repricing: resolve product definition, verify exact installed basis, load its bootstrap entrypoint then Goals or bound work-wave carrier; perform Goals-to-Intent and confirm/write Intent, Intent-to-Product and confirm/write present product bridge; gather constitutional requirement sources, derive/write the live requirement surface, choosing individual files or grouped families for clarity without monolithic sprawl. Establish sole live requirement authority before design/code, prefer declarative structure, and record remaining major ambiguity before downstream realisation. For a real-use gap: triage/classify first, write the scenario as the first substantive project artifact, then analyse cause preserving alternatives evidence cannot separate; re-enter at the selected class and flow forward, introducing Goals/Intent only for changed wave/direction/scope. Intake source never bypasses this sequence.
constraints.uncertainty: The register describes the revised gap procedure as proposed and pending product-owner acceptance.

conditions: A major boundary is reached or an operational lifecycle phase remains unanswered.

grounding.quote:
Ambiguity detection is
mandatory; blocking is policy

constraints.statement: Always surface and govern major ambiguity; never hide it in informal operator judgment, ambient precedent or silent model choice. At each major boundary record remaining/new ambiguity, affected invariant/asset/decision boundary, decision if proceeding, and outcome resolved/carried/escalated/blocked. For the exact-basis resolution predicate, only resolved is satisfied; later dependent claims cannot treat carried, escalated or blocked as resolved. Unanswered lifecycle phases are recorded gaps, never silent absences. Profile runtime shorthands stay in their own context unless an explicit relation imports/translates them.
constraints.uncertainty: Core values for the three non-resolved outcomes are delegated to ACTIVATION and not supplied.

conditions: Release identity, dependency basis or live truth is represented.

grounding.quote:
it is not an exact dependency, evidence or constitutional
basis and cannot silently change a consumer selection.

constraints.statement: An immutable cut is point-in-time accepted-feature-set identity in release metadata/process evaluation, not live project specification. The mutable version selector is not an exact dependency/evidence/constitutional basis and cannot silently change consumer selection. Shared realisation surfaces should describe current truth by role, boundary and status rather than release-line labels. Release criteria/publication/advancement/cutting and successor conservation belong to RELEASE; project constitutional version boundaries belong to PRODUCT_DEFINITION. Calculus, interpretation and encoding retain independent identities, judgments, supersession and proof obligations; none automatically becomes an independently released Product.
constraints.uncertainty: Referenced release and specification-surface rules are not supplied in full.

conditions: Method law is adopted or propagated.

grounding.quote: it requires its own Product authorisation

constraints.statement: Maintain the stated causal authority chain. A tool, runtime, carrier schema or assurance implementation cannot enter merely by accompanying a method lesson; each needs its own Product authorisation. Other standards consume admitted law by reference. Consumers select a complete released version rather than mixing members from different cuts.

conditions: A core interface changes.
exceptions: Bounded product-slice proof remains governed by path-relative promotion.

grounding.quote:
run complete migration-closure proof only after the migration
wave is complete

constraints.statement: Change the authoritative core contract first, ban bridge code as an authoritative surface for the family, audit every producer and consumer, migrate each to the new contract and follow every downstream effect until no superseded closure law remains. Complete migration-closure proof follows the completed wave. Declaring complete a split state of old/new producers, discrepant runtime/reporting/topology carriers, authoritative aliases, second-truth projections or merely green tests is forbidden.

conditions: Selecting a strategy for core-interface or major implementation replacement.
exceptions: The evolution presumption does not require unsafe or constitutionally inadmissible predecessor paths or mechanisms explicitly superseded by product authority.

grounding.quote:
Fundamental re-adoption requires explicit selection by the human authority
owning the affected product boundary.

constraints.statement: Where evolution and re-adoption are both lawful/feasible and a working predecessor can reach the admitted outcome without competing or ambiguous authority, presume bounded evolution rebuttably, conserving accepted semantics and feedback. Core migration within evolution uses inside-out hard breaks. Fundamental re-adoption needs explicit selection by the human owner, comparison against evolution on product value, feedback latency, authority risk, reversibility, total cost and retained predecessor semantics, and a bounded abort/re-entry condition. Scale or architectural preference alone does not select it.

conditions: Either migration strategy is used or a product outcome is promoted.
exceptions: Outside-path residual material may be deferred only under all stated deferment conditions.

grounding.quote:
If the same request, fact, identity, state or projection is
admissible to old and new authority, authority is competing and promotion
blocks

constraints.statement: No proxy/partial interface stands in for the new contract in any acceptance path, and no bridge/fallback remains silently authoritative. Promotion requires singular unambiguous authority across the full affected causal closure; competing authority blocks that outcome. Outside-path superseded-family material may be deferred only if explicitly non-authoritative for the outcome or authoritative solely for specified disjoint product/compatibility scope with deterministic routing, unable to falsify current or retained product claims, and carrying a bounded migration/qualification/release disposition. Tests are leak detectors and proof surfaces, not the migration plan.

conditions: An intermediate outcome is promoted before migration completion, or work continues after slice acceptance.

grounding.quote:
ticket activity alone is not that
basis.

constraints.statement: Intermediate promotion requires singular path authority and compliant residual deferment; it neither closes migration nor waives final retirement. Ticket/review wording cannot narrow slice authority. Active migration status does not renew exhausted slice growth authority: already-admitted removal, demotion and migration-closure proof may continue within their bound without further product-progress claims; further material producer/consumer growth requires another still-live basis admitted under §3. Accepted slices name what they close, keep enclosing migration visibly open, and project no migration, qualification or release closure.
constraints.uncertainty: The §3 admission basis for renewed growth is not supplied.

conditions: Every core-interface migration.

grounding.quote:
Temporary scaffolding
is lawful only if it is explicitly non-authoritative and scheduled for
removal before closure

constraints.statement: Explicitly declare exact affected scope; every excluded/disjoint product or compatibility scope and deterministic routing; new authoritative contract; superseded contract/surface; new authoritative closure law; full old/new producer and consumer sets; and every derived projection, report, status and proof surface. Classify every old path remove, replace, re-authorize or temporary scaffolding. Temporary scaffolding must be explicitly non-authoritative and scheduled for removal before closure.

conditions: A core-interface migration.
exceptions: An explicit live-product compatibility feature with an intentionally specified, explicitly bounded path clearly identified as compatibility rather than current native truth.

grounding.quote:
The only lawful exception is an explicit compatibility
feature retained as part of the live product

constraints.statement: No compatibility alias remains authoritative; no fallback identity law remains silent runtime behaviour; no bridge participates in acceptance as the new contract; no old reader/writer remains authoritative for an outcome once the new contract governs it; and no proxy/partial implementation standing between old and new truth counts as completion.

conditions: Migration closure is considered.

grounding.quote:
if the authoritative carrier can close while a
projection still depends on an older law, the migration is incomplete.

constraints.statement: Views cannot become second closure surfaces. Migration remains incomplete if runtime, reporting, topology and proof can disagree because they use different carriers or laws; if a projection independently closes while its authoritative carrier remains open; or if that carrier closes while a projection still depends on older law.

conditions: An inside-out hard-break migration.
exceptions: Isolated non-authoritative downstream exploration is permitted subject to the publication/admission boundary.

grounding.quote:
A
downstream projection ticket does not close while the source-carrier
ticket it depends on is still open.

constraints.statement: Discover the full best-guess interface family before using proof for closure, including producers, consumers, projections, prompts, reports, wrappers, replay/ingest/bootstrap paths and proof surfaces. Authoritative producer/source-carrier work precedes consumer, projection, prompt, dossier, report and review hardening. Downstream exploration must remain isolated and non-authoritative and cannot land in public runtime/projection/prompt/report/proof entrypoints before source-carrier publication and admission. Dependent projection tickets cannot close while source-carrier tickets remain open; dependency direction must expose this order.

conditions: Each hard break in the migration wave.
exceptions: Explicitly repriced-upward work may leave the original wave; specified deterministically routed non-overlapping product/compatibility scopes may coexist while migration stays open.

grounding.quote:
run negative proof that the
severed seam is rejected rather than merely unused.

constraints.statement: Publish/admit the new deepest source carrier; deliberately sever one old authoritative seam and keep it broken; repair outward through consumers, projections, prompts/reports and proof surfaces; provide negative proof of rejection, not mere non-use. Tests may find missed interfaces but cannot replace inventory. Newly found affected interfaces remain in the wave absent explicit upward repricing. Re-enabling the seam through wrappers, fallbacks, projections or prompts is a migration defect; the wave never permits competing or ambiguous dual truth for the same request, fact, identity, state or projection.

conditions: Migration proof or downstream hardening is claimed.
exceptions: Bounded slice proof can establish only the exact intermediate outcome permitted by path-relative promotion.

grounding.quote:
per-break proof shows the severed old seam is rejected or fails closed
before downstream hardening can count as progress.

constraints.statement: Complete migration-closure proof is invalid while producers/consumers remain split between contracts. Slice proof cannot establish migration closure. Tests passing because bridge semantics persist and green local tests over split architecture do not prove closure. Complete proof follows migration; per-break rejection/fail-closed proof precedes counting downstream hardening as progress.

conditions: Completion is claimed across the declared affected scope.
exceptions: A superseded mechanism may be retained for a distinct supported responsibility under the retention requirements.

grounding.quote:
Until those conditions hold the
work remains an active migration wave, not a completed refactor

constraints.statement: Completion requires every authoritative producer writing and consumer reading the new contract; retirement or justified distinct retention of superseded authoritative paths; downstream projections of the same truth; one closure law shared by runtime/reporting/topology/proof; and no temporary scaffolding in acceptance. Retention bears the burden: each retained mechanism identifies current supported obligation, owner, purpose, execution scope and material cost. Temporary compatibility/comparison has expiry/removal trigger. Tests, oracle labels or nominal demotion do not justify duplicate production responsibility. A required cold reconstruction route or independent oracle may meet an enduring distinct obligation without invented expiry. Identify the surviving owner of surviving obligations; require no replacement guard where no governing basis exists. Retirement in a closed affected cone need not await unrelated whole-product closure.

conditions: A fundamental migration is selected.

grounding.quote: nothing carries forward by default,

constraints.statement: Treat inherited constitutional documents as source material, not new-line law. Explicitly re-adopt every retained statement, requirement, design choice and guide rule; carry-forward should land in its correct Goals/Intent/Product/Requirements/Design/guide/template layer. Old code/design governs only if re-derived and re-adopted; absence means not yet adopted. Classify every inherited module, interface, carrier, projection and proof surface before reuse; unclassified implementation is a defect. Declare the migration line, establish fresh method/Goals/Intent/Product/Requirements/Design surfaces, move old implementation sideways if needed to prevent ambient authority, classify constitutional and implementation material separately, copy only intended retention and re-derive design/code from new surfaces. carry_across is explicit re-adoption, not automatic copying. Direct runtime/projection/prompt/proof/review dependence on the sideways line is bridge debt; partial proxy dependence is not lawful closure. A new constitutional surface is lawful supersession, not silent mutation of the old surface.

conditions: Inherited requirements or other constitutional material are classified.

grounding.quote: The two relate as follows, and are not one classification:

constraints.statement: Constitutional adoption decision and live requirement standing are distinct. An adopted requirement enters Active, or Deferred when adopted as explicitly not-yet-operative. Deferred adoption leaves the requirement outside the live surface with no legacy classification or authority. Superseded/orphaned inherited requirements take Superseded/Orphaned with the referenced table's meanings. Other inherited constitutional material retains adoption classes/steps. These are declared states of new-line surfaces and neither constitute nor supply RELEASE successor dispositions of predecessor claims.
constraints.uncertainty: The detailed legacy-classification meanings are absent, and the source register contains a conflicting compression of this distinction.

conditions: A wave is in flight or lands across its declared affected scope.
exceptions: An intentional compatibility feature may remain when named as current product behaviour, justified in specification, scope-bounded and tested.

grounding.quote:
Otherwise the correct action is
deletion, not passive preservation.

constraints.statement: During flight, mixed implementation may exist only below the current break boundary as explicitly non-authoritative plumbing; adapters/scaffolds must be named, bounded and outside acceptance. Prior-model traces never supply competing/ambiguous authority for the same request/fact/identity/state/projection. Explicit deterministic non-overlapping product/compatibility scopes may coexist while migration remains visibly open. At landing only the new operative surface remains live for the affected scope; erase prior operative paths, retaining journey history only in version control, events and superseded records. Mixed operative models are not a stable end state.

conditions: A construction step is configured or run under the described method.

grounding.quote: the re-entry conditions are the change classes of §4.

constraints.statement: Use the working tenant's computational calculus, execution environment and binding resource limits. Bind selected outcome to the §3 product outcome/prerequisite/experiment, owning relations to constitutional layers, and re-entry to §4 classes. ACTIVATION owns work admission, qualification, proportionality and configuration. Configuration determines construction/assessment/disposition frames and return consumer from task operations, dependencies, capabilities and assurance; this member adds no role inventory, coordinator or sequence. If present, a coordinator acts within decision grant and selects next authorised action. Executive/Worker/Reviewer is one profile configuration and governs only where selected.
constraints.uncertainty: Referenced generic construction, admission, qualification and configuration rules are not supplied.

conditions: Delivery priority or sequencing is selected.

grounding.quote:
This is a priority relation, not a fixed
global execution sequence or a scheduling runtime

This is a
sequencing heuristic for any realisation, not law;

constraints.statement: Apply proportionality to product outcome, likelihood, impact, reversibility, dependency and delayed-feedback cost. Probability informs priority without waiving authority, integrity, safety, retained release claims or hard stops; numeric confidence without support remains unresolved under quantified assurance. Default priority exposes/advances the smallest supported path and highest-value likely failures. Displacing defensive/prerequisite work identifies affected claim, evidence, bounded effort, return condition and expected product consequence. Early smallest-real-path delivery and widening by consequential uncertainty, interface reach and failure impact are heuristics, not universal law; a passing path establishes only exercised relations, and selected baseline steel-thread law remains profile-owned.

conditions: Constitutional claims are proved in practice.

grounding.quote:
The rules that govern how constitutional claims are proved in practice are
tier-1 law:

constraints.statement: EVALUATION owns target identity/adequacy, semantic/evidence/projection separation, assurance congruence and method qualification. ASSURANCE owns verification layers, testing taxonomy and fixture/proof portability, test authority, scenario bundles, installed-development proof and significant-path coverage. Apply the listed authority trace, realisation proof, conditional negative proof and current residual-pressure evidence under the existing TICKETS closure condition.
constraints.uncertainty: These owner laws and their detailed tests are not present.

conditions: An ADR is authored, superseded, retired or changes tenant scope.
exceptions: A superseded ADR may be deleted only when explicitly retired.

grounding.quote:
a superseded ADR is deleted only when it is explicitly
retired.

constraints.statement: Each ADR explicitly includes Status (active/superseded/retired), Implements requirement IDs, Derives from intent ID or strategy document, Supersedes prior ADR/doctrine, Superseded by successor when superseded, and Retained special case when earlier behaviour is intentionally retained. Name an operational mechanism named by its requirement; immediately reprice the event-contract ADR when event taxonomy expands. Preserve superseded ADR in place with status and successor. When shared/cross-tenant scope narrows to one tenant, move the ADR to that tenant's design surface and record the move in supersession history. This member owns these lifecycle/location rules formerly present only in templates.

conditions: An ADR is stored or named.

grounding.quote:
ADRs are not placed in comments, generated views,
runtime archives or requirement folders.

constraints.statement: Store ADRs at the closest design surface owning the decision. Tenant-local ADRs use the product-bound tenant surface; shared/cross-tenant ADRs the common surface; non-tenanted/project-local ADRs their governing design surface. Defaults are build_tenants/<tenant-path>/design/adrs/, build_tenants/common/design/adrs/ and <governing-design-surface>/adrs/. Registry entries record actual tenant identities/locations for every layout. Follow ADR-<local-id>-short-slug.md with local ID unique in the owning adrs directory. Each ADR remains source truth; a registry can drift unless maintained.

conditions: A tenant selects or changes its means of realisation.

grounding.quote:
Author identity, actor identity and
   operation kind stay distinct, and none determines another.

constraints.statement: The tenant owns binding, realisation and evidence while WHAT meaning remains fixed. Selection must satisfy every requirement, including human decisions and independent assessments; executor convenience removes neither. Author identity, actor identity and operation kind are distinct and mutually non-determining. One actor may perform several kinds only under each kind's grant. Human participation alone gives no authority/adjudication; the admitted person takes a reserved human decision. Stack/human/mixed selection belongs in design and narrows executable realisation class; major ambiguity is recorded/governed. Binding changes enter intake and receive a class; needing weaker obligations requires WHAT change at its owner, never unilateral tenant choice.

conditions: A binding serves selected obligations or limits an activation.

grounding.quote:
A resource claim without its unit or its boundary supports no
   conformance claim.

constraints.statement: Identify operations with inputs, outputs, effects and outcome values, each outcome mapping to exactly one core value; record intended external effects including uncertain completion under ACTIVATION. Identify composition laws, permitted transformations, resource measures and operational assumptions, including actors/tools/availability/failure. Measure human effort, elapsed time, communication and machine resources where obligations need them; each measure gives unit, counted scope and start/stop boundary. Measure selected context against actor capacity under ACTIVATION. Execution binding states time/spend/other limit values and measurable units/boundaries before the activation; configurations take resource limits and failure assumptions from it.
constraints.uncertainty: The full result map, effect model, context measure and limit law are referenced externally.

conditions: Binding conformance is assessed.

grounding.quote:
the binding's conformance for that
   obligation is `falsified`;

constraints.statement: Requirements determine fitness; executor kind alone neither accepts nor rejects. Evidence must show required meaning/constraints and applicable authority, independence, failure and recovery conditions. Each assessment returns a predicate-specific core value; tenant conformance is their conjunction with requirement obligations as coverage. Merging required independent assessments or automating a required human decision falsifies the weakened obligation; the lost assessment/decision has no applicable closed result in such a run. Matching outputs, lower cost and speed cannot discharge loss. Categorical-structure preservation is a further formally discharged claim, distinct on the equivalence ladder. Structural validation of an a_c representation selects no executor and proves no execution conformance, including for a human-process model.
constraints.uncertainty: Full conjunction, formal-fragment and equivalence-ladder rules are not supplied.

conditions: A calculus is reused, accounts are mapped, or several tenants are developed.

grounding.quote:
A mapping from one account to
   another is a transformation:

constraints.statement: Reuse a computational calculus across tenants/environments only where each binding satisfies and demonstrates its laws. A different language/tool/team/person alone does not require a different calculus; replacing an executor while laws hold changes execution binding. Keep algorithmic, informational and computational accounts distinct. Account mappings state preservation, licensing law and exactness or approximation with adequacy relation/end-to-end bound, discharged under ACTIVATION refinement; a_c recording follows AC-013. The binding identifies joined accounts and environment evidence. Branches, workcopies, territories, review/merge mechanics are project-local law bound in product definition or tenant design, not prescribed here; tenant ticket-lifecycle independence and review remain TICKETS requirements.
constraints.uncertainty: Account definitions, refinement law and multi-tenant ticket details are outside the supplied source.

conditions: The register's supersession statements are interpreted.

grounding.quote: superseded in the gap procedure, proposed and pending the product owner's acceptance:

constraints.statement: Preserve proposed, pending-product-owner-acceptance status for: spec-drivenness condition 11, limiting source-repricing failure to drift diagnosed in constitutional source, with other twelve conditions conserved; constitutional-chain repricing, using class-selected re-entry and Goals/Intent only for changed wave/direction/scope; renewal opening/diagram/generative rule with the same re-entry change; persistent-delta and tenth drift signals, adding predictive-model/observation causes and replacing mandatory new Intent with lawful Requirements-or-upstream re-entry, with eight other signals conserved; and the gap procedure's triage-selected cause/re-entry instead of the predecessor's constitutional/implementation split. These are source proposals, not established acceptance.
constraints.uncertainty: No product-owner acceptance is supplied.

grounding.quote:
The two family tables at §2 and §4 decide nothing beyond the
rules they cite;

constraints.statement: Treat recorded generalisations as authored changes: graph functions→functions, reconciliation graph→design/module, graph-native→realisation meaning, UX_METHOD→a profile, concrete Goals/Intent/Product/requirements paths→surfaces, installed STDO basis→installed basis, REQ/INT prefixes→generic identifiers, overlay fields→WHAT bindings/tenant registry/design/common surfaces, runtime shorthand→profile-owned shorthand, traversal binding→PROFILES, Prime→design-profile prime law, co-evolution predicate without symbol, and Product authorization→authorisation. The design-profile core rule retains should force and scope; its non-goals retain non-requirements, readability and required composition/effect algebra while vocabulary stays optional. The register labels §11 largely new except conserved tenant/WHAT determinations; new distinctions include facts/states versus results, successor-disposition separation and admitted human-adjudication semantics. Family tables add no decisions and their format is FOUNDATION-owned. The predecessor evidence-rules heading is marked inapplicable as naming children only; its children are disposed separately.
constraints.uncertainty: Predecessor bodies and several receiving sections are absent; conservation assertions cannot be independently established.

grounding.quote: only; nothing here depends on that cut to be applied.

constraints.statement: TICKETS clauses name requiring P0–P6 principles and its mechanisms could be realised differently under the same principles. SPEC_METHOD owns the recorded change classes; ACTIVATION owns step-side admission; EVALUATION owns generic claims, independent assessment and acceptance; ASSURANCE owns testing. TICKETS does not duplicate these laws. Its family F13 opens §5. rc.2 anchors point to predecessor TICKET_METHOD only for provenance, not an application dependency.
constraints.uncertainty: Most referenced TICKETS mechanics beyond the supplied excerpt remain unavailable.

conditions: A sprint contains work or discovers debt at close.

grounding.quote:
it does not erase the need for paydown tickets when close review finds debt
that must survive past the sprint

constraints.statement: Use durable tickets for work needing cross-session identity and manifest-local entries for small changes whose only independent value is sprint traceability. A sprint may contain either or both, but close-discovered debt that outlives it requires paydown tickets. Sprint closure requires explicit sprint-close review under cited project and SPEC_METHOD authority.

conditions: Work is prepared for execution through a contract.

grounding.quote:
execution may proceed in the same invocation
under the admitted contract; closure is checked against that same contract;

constraints.statement: The intended loop selects the smallest lawful lifetime carrier, has an agent draft one run-scoped contract, and validates/admit-or-rejects classification against deterministic criteria under ACTIVATION admission. Log the admitted basis into runtime/event truth, assemble prompts from admitted work law rather than raw phrasing, and evaluate closure against the same admitted criteria. Execution may follow admission in the same invocation; resulting state still follows proof, gap analysis and repricing. Drafting alone is not admission.
constraints.uncertainty: The admission criteria and runtime mechanisms are not provided here.

conditions: A milestone or ticket is considered complete.

grounding.quote: Commentary and generated summaries cannot mutate milestone or ticket truth

constraints.statement: Milestone acceptance proves only its declared claim; accepted design does not satisfy implementation, installed proof, qualification or release. Every closure-bearing milestone must be accepted under condition-based closure for its own claim before ticket completion. Optional/deferred work needs an explicit disposition and owner. Commentary/generated summaries cannot mutate milestone or ticket truth.
constraints.uncertainty: The full §7 closure condition is not supplied.

conditions: Carrier locations or board views are selected.
exceptions: A board becomes source truth only through explicit product-definition rebinding of ticket authority with no rival remaining.

grounding.quote: There is no separate mandatory `ACTIVE_TASKS.md` in this model.

their
absence from the project tree is not absence from the governing method.

constraints.statement: Resolve POSTING_GUIDE and TICKETS from the product definition's exact shared installed basis; absent project-tree files do not imply absent method law. ACTIVE_TASKS.md is not mandatory. An optional generated board derives from bound ticket authority and remains a projection unless explicitly rebound with no rival.
constraints.uncertainty: Installed-basis resolution and complete rebinding law are referenced externally.

conditions: A carrier substitutes for the selected default.

grounding.quote:
neither growth
changes the authority or refusal laws

constraints.statement: The durable local-file model remains valid whenever selected. Other carriers need not reproduce folders but preserve ticket authority and one-durable-record refusal laws. A tracker holding tickets is lawful only through explicit product-definition rebinding with no rival. Alternative sprint carriers preserve identity, required fields, history, closure law and one truth; integrations and projections never silently change authority or refusal.
constraints.uncertainty: The full ticket one-record refusal law lies outside the supplied excerpt.

conditions: Every sprint manifest.

grounding.quote: Each sprint manifest records at least `id`, `title`, `status`, `goal`,

constraints.statement: Record at least id, title, status, goal, opened_at, updated_at, authority_refs, scope, excluded_boundaries, expected_change_classes, included_tickets or iterations, closure_trigger, closure_law, proof_surface, deferred_compliance, non_closure_conditions and paydown_policy. authority_refs identifies upstream governing surfaces; excluded_boundaries identifies forbidden changes, typically product truth, data contracts, runtime semantics, governance/closure law, public carrier shape and release criteria. deferred_compliance identifies intentionally deferred local proof/review/accessibility/screenshots/walkthroughs/tests/design wording/trace cleanup; paydown_policy states acceptance, ticketing, repricing or removal at close.

conditions: Work enters a sprint.
exceptions: Manifest-local iterations may rely on the sprint's declared class only while inside scope and excluded boundaries.

grounding.quote: It may not batch away intake triage:

constraints.statement: Admission requires a manifest making the boundary reviewable: bounded scope, cited authority, expected classes, explicit exclusions, closure law, non-closure conditions and paydown policy. Repeated closure criteria may be batched, but substantive included tickets still record lawful change_class and re_entry_point. Manifest-local reliance on a declared class is conditional and never removes intake triage.

conditions: Local compliance proof is deferred.

grounding.quote:
the expected correction cost is lower than the per-change proof
cost;

constraints.statement: Defer only if the manifest names the proof/cleanup class, debt is local to admitted surface, expected correction costs less than per-change proof, the sprint is short enough for reviewability, and close review classifies/pays down debt. It is never silent debt or closure before paid down, accepted or repriced. If forbidden law-changing content appears, record it and exit the sprint path through a standalone ticket, repricing or sprint supersession.

batch work, coordinate tickets or iteration entries, price proof cost and
